steps.text: Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Add potato and cook until tender but still firm, about 15 minutes. Drain, cool, and chop.
Sauté onion and garlic in a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat. When onion is soft, stir in spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium and pour in eggs. Cook until the bottom has set, about 2 minutes. Stir in potatoes and tomatoes.
Season with salt, pepper, cayenne, and hot sauce. Cook, stirring occasionally, until eggs have set. Sprinkle with grated cheese and serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Egg Scramble
raw_recipe.description: This egg scramble recipe is a perfect mix of veggies topped with cheese and hot sauce. You can use any variety of spice and skip the cheese.
raw_recipe.name: Egg Scramble

review.reviewBody: I used a medium sized organic red potato (I did dice it before cooking, just to make it a little easier), a sweet onion, two free range egg whites/two full eggs, Romanita tomatoes and 2% sharp cheddar cheese. My kids didn't care for it but I reallu thought it was great. I had a little homemade salsa over the top and it was quite filling. YUM! NOTE: I did use just a touch of butter to "oil" my pan, but you can use non stick low-cal spray or EVOO, if you'd rather. Shoot, bacon grease would be good, too!

This was a very savory breakfast. I only had large baking potatoes, so I peeled one, cut it in half and cooked it, because it wouldn't fit in the pot whole. I scaled this in half as I only needed a couple of servings. I only used half the potato. I did add the diced cooked potato in with the onion and garlic to get a little color on the bits. The spinach was a nice addition, and added some color, but didn't look very pretty in the dish after wilting. Every now and then I got a sharp bite from the onion which I didn't like. I'd also leave the tomatoes out, as they were soft and wet and made a weird texture. I think this would benefit from the addition of some savory meat such as sausage. I'm not certain how I feel about garlic in the breakfast eggs. It was ... different, not good, not bad, just different. The pinch of cayenne was nice and added that little something extra. While this was fine, it wasn't really my thing, so I'd pass on this again.

Very tasty recipe! I diced two smaller organic red skin potatoes (with skins on) and sauteed them first in a little butter until browned and soft. I then added the onions, followed by some grated, fresh garlic. I substituted some fresh, chopped swiss chard because that's what I had on hand. A few dashes of cayenne pepper and a dash of hot sauce gave this dish a nice flavor without being too spicy. I had some organic, raw cheddar cheese to top this off with, which was really the "icing on the cake". 

Can't wait to make this again!!

Yummy! I browned the potatoes in the pan with the onion and left out the cayenne and hot sauce. I garnished the egg scramble with fresh chopped green onions (left them in larger chunks for some crunch).

This is really good and really healthy. I added some chopped yellow pepper because it was either add it to this or throw it away! I browned my potoatoes a little before adding the spinach and added my tomato in last - I hate mushy warm tomatoes in my eggs. I forgot to top this with cheese, but it was still good without.

Salmon and eggs for Hubs this morning, but this for me! I left out the potato, cooked up some diced bacon, then continued with the recipe, leaving out the cayenne. LOVED it - the combination of ingredients and flavors (garlic is great in this!) were right up my alley. Being colorful and super-nutritious doesn't hurt either. I think the bacon, however, had a lot to do with the success of this for me!

Didn't have any spinach so added some broccoli, califlower and green pepper, also some cummun seed and fresh licorice basil. very yummy not 4 servings though more like two. Cooked it in my cast iron skillet. Didn't boil potatoes just diced them up.

Fantastic recipe - easy to make and tastes great. Like others I also added some bacon pieces which tasted good. I tripled the amount of spinach which went well, but as I like more greens, will be adding even more next time. Will definitely be making this again!

A very good idea that fit with the random food items I had lying about the apartment. A way to give it slightly more flavor is, instead of boiling the potato, dice into very small pieces and brown along with the onions and a bit of salt before adding the garlic. I suppose it changes the texture slightly, but the browning on the potato and slight caramelization of the onion adds a lot.
Delightful! Left out the potato, used red onion to add some extra colour, and used kale from my garden instead of spinach.
Great for an easy breakfast! I had a leftover grilled potato that I wanted to use up and instead of the spinach I added some green pepper - very tasty.
I skipped potato and added crispy bacon. My husband loved it. It was delicious. Thanks for the great recipe.
Terrific
No changes made. I will make again.
Instead of cheddar, I make this with spicy pepper jack. Otherwise it would be a bit bland for me.
Great for a quick breakfast. Well boiled potatoes are the trick. ????
I substituted lettuce for the spinach and pasta for the potatoes. Also skipped the hot sauce
Delicious!! Lo Carb, fresh veggies-yum!! Boiled potato for a little bit longer as per prior review, otherwise made as per recipe. It's a keeper in our house!
ok, won't make again
